short_description.id: Yakusanoikazuchi adalah nama kolektif delapan kami petir dalam mitologi, yang menurut Kojiki bersemayam di jasad Izanami di Yomi dan mengejar Izanagi.
short_description.en: Yakusanoikazuchi is the collective name of the eight thunder kami in mythology, which in the Kojiki dwell in Izanami's corpse in Yomi and pursue Izanagi.

long_description.id: Yakusanoikazuchi adalah nama kolektif delapan kami petir. Para dewa itu mewakili berbagai bentuk badai. Unsur ikazuchi (雷) berarti petir. Delapan kami ini mencakup, antara lain, Fusu-ikazuchi, Hono-ikazuchi, dan Ō-ikazuchi.
long_description.en: Yakusanoikazuchi is the collective name of eight thunder kami. The deities represent different forms of storm. The element ikazuchi (雷) means thunder. The eight include Fusu-ikazuchi, Hono-ikazuchi and Ō-ikazuchi, among others.

long_description.id: Menurut Ensiklopedia Shinto, kedelapan kami petir membusuk di dalam jasad Izanami seperti dilihat Izanagi di Yomi. Kojiki menempatkan petir pada kepala, dada, perut, kemaluan, kedua tangan, dan kedua kaki Izanami, sedangkan satu tulisan alternatif Nihongi memberi penempatan dan sebagian nama yang berbeda. Satu tafsir menyejajarkan kelahiran delapan petir ini dengan delapan kami dari tubuh Kagutsuchi.
long_description.en: According to the Encyclopedia of Shinto, the eight thunder kami festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by Izanagi in Yomi. The Kojiki places thunders in Izanami's head, breast, belly, genitals, both hands and both legs, while an alternate writing in the Nihongi gives a different placement and some different names. One interpretation parallels the birth of these eight thunders with the eight kami from the body of Kagutsuchi.

long_description.id: Menurut beberapa penuturan, para dewa itu berasal dari belatung jasad Izanami yang membusuk. Setelah Izanagi melihat jasad Izanami dan melarikan diri ketakutan, Izanami mengirim Yomotsu-shikome, 150 pendekar, dan delapan kami petir mengejarnya. Menurut ensiklopedia, Izanagi melempar buah persik gaib di Yomotsuhirasaka dan mengusir para pengejar. Kojiki menempatkan Petir Hitam di perut Izanami, sedangkan Nihon Shoki menempatkannya di dubur.
long_description.en: Some tellings say the eight deities came from the maggots of Izanami's rotting corpse. After Izanagi saw Izanami's corpse and escaped in horror, Izanami dispatched the Yomotsu-shikome, 150 warriors, together with the eight thunder kami to pursue him. According to the encyclopedia, Izanagi threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka and dispersed his pursuers. The Kojiki places Black Thunder in Izanami's belly, while the Nihon Shoki places it in her rectum.

cultural_context.id: Menurut ensiklopedia, delapan adalah angka suci tetapi di sini mungkin berarti "sangat banyak", dan delapan petir sejajar dengan delapan kami dari tubuh Kagutsuchi.
cultural_context.en: According to the encyclopedia, eight is a sacred number but here may mean "a great many", and the eight thunders parallel the eight kami from Kagutsuchi's body.

who.en: The eight thunder kami of mythology.

summary.en: After Izanagi sees Izanami's corpse and flees, Izanami sends pursuers including the eight thunder kami; Izanagi throws down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka and disperses them.

description.en: The "Even Pass of Yomi", where Izanagi throws magical peaches to disperse his pursuers.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa Kojiki dan Nihongi menempatkan petir pada bagian tubuh Izanami yang berbeda?
learning_questions.en: Why do the Kojiki and the Nihongi place the thunders on different parts of Izanami's body?

claims.quote: Yakusanoikazuchi or ikazuchi is a collective name for the eight kami of thunder in Japanese mythology.

statement.id: Yakusanoikazuchi adalah nama kolektif delapan kami petir.
statement.en: Yakusanoikazuchi is the collective name of eight thunder kami.

claims.quote: Each one represents a different type of storm.

statement.id: Para dewa itu mewakili berbagai bentuk badai.
statement.en: The deities represent different forms of storm.

claims.quote: Ikazuchi (雷) literally means thunder in Japanese.
Some tellings say that the eight deities were from the maggots of Izanami's rotting corpse.

statement.id: Beberapa penuturan menyebut kedelapan dewa itu berasal dari belatung jasad Izanami yang membusuk.
statement.en: Some tellings say the eight deities came from the maggots of Izanami's rotting corpse.

claims.quote: Many versions of the Nihon Shoki and the Kojiki state that after Izanagi saw his wife in such a state and fled in terror, Izanami sent the Yomotsu-shikome, 150 warriors, and the eight thunder kami after him.

statement.id: Mereka mengejar Izanagi ketika ia melarikan diri dari alam kematian.
statement.en: They pursue Izanagi when he flees the underworld.

claims.quote: Kuro-ikazuchi: (Black thunder) The Kojiki says that this deity came from Izanami's belly.

statement.id: Kojiki menempatkan Petir Hitam di perut Izanami.
statement.en: The Kojiki places Black Thunder in Izanami’s belly.

claims.quote: However, the Nihon Shoki says that Kuro-ikazuchi was in Izanami's rectum.

statement.id: Nihon Shoki justru menempatkan Petir Hitam di duburnya.
statement.en: The Nihon Shoki instead places Black Thunder in her rectum.

claims.quote: [Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami] (Kojiki) The "eight kinds of thunder kami" that festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by her consort Izanagi in the underworld of Yomi.

statement.id: Menurut Ensiklopedia Shinto, Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami dalam Kojiki adalah "delapan jenis kami petir" yang membusuk di dalam jasad Izanami, seperti dilihat suaminya Izanagi di dunia bawah Yomi.
statement.en: According to the Encyclopedia of Shinto, the Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami of the Kojiki are the "eight kinds of thunder kami" that festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by her consort Izanagi in the underworld of Yomi.

claims.quote: According to Kojiki, in her head was the "great thunder," in her breast was the "fire thunder," in her belly was the "black thunder," in her genitals was the "cleft thunder," in her left hand was the "young thunder," in the right hand was the "earth thunder," in her left leg was the "sounding thunder," and in her right leg was the "reposing thunder."

statement.id: Menurut Kojiki, kedelapan petir itu berada di kepala (petir besar), dada (petir api), perut (petir hitam), kemaluan (petir belah), tangan kiri (petir muda), tangan kanan (petir tanah), kaki kiri (petir bergema), dan kaki kanan (petir beristirahat) Izanami.
statement.en: According to the Kojiki, the eight thunders were in the corpse's head (great thunder), breast (fire thunder), belly (black thunder), genitals (cleft thunder), left hand (young thunder), right hand (earth thunder), left leg (sounding thunder) and right leg (reposing thunder).

claims.quote: An "alternate writing" transmitted by Nihongi, however, states that "great thunder" was in her head, "fire thunder" was in her breast, "earth thunder" was in her belly, "young thunder" was in her back, "black thunder" was in her rectum, "mountain thunder" was in her hands, "field thunder" was in her feet, and "cleft thunder" was in her genitals.

statement.id: Satu "tulisan alternatif" dalam Nihongi menyebut petir besar di kepala, petir api di dada, petir tanah di perut, petir muda di punggung, petir hitam di dubur, petir gunung di tangan, petir ladang di kaki, dan petir belah di kemaluan.
statement.en: An "alternate writing" transmitted by the Nihongi states that great thunder was in her head, fire thunder in her breast, earth thunder in her belly, young thunder in her back, black thunder in her rectum, mountain thunder in her hands, field thunder in her feet and cleft thunder in her genitals.

claims.quote: Of the eight thunders, three have the same name and place in the two accounts, three agree in name only, and the remaining two are different.

statement.id: Dari delapan petir itu, tiga memiliki nama dan tempat yang sama dalam dua catatan, tiga hanya sama namanya, dan dua sisanya berbeda.
statement.en: Of the eight thunders, three have the same name and place in the two accounts, three agree in name only, and the remaining two are different.

claims.quote: The fact that eight thunders were produced in Izanami's dead body parallels the fact that eight kami were produced from the dismembered body of the fire kami Kagutsuchi. While eight is considered a sacred number, it is here likely used merely to denote "a great many."

statement.id: Lahirnya delapan petir dari jasad Izanami disamakan dengan lahirnya delapan kami dari tubuh Kagutsuchi yang terpotong; delapan dianggap angka suci, tetapi di sini mungkin hanya berarti "sangat banyak".
statement.en: The eight thunders produced in Izanami's dead body parallel the eight kami produced from the dismembered body of the fire kami Kagutsuchi; eight is considered a sacred number but is here likely used merely to denote "a great many".

claims.quote: According to the various Kojiki and Nihongi accounts mentioned above, Izanami ordered the "hags of Yomi" and the eight thunder kami to chase Izanagi ... Izanagi, however, threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka (the "Even Pass of Yomi"), and thus dispersed his pursuers.

statement.id: Menurut berbagai catatan Kojiki dan Nihongi, Izanami memerintahkan "nenek-nenek Yomi" dan delapan kami petir mengejar Izanagi; Izanagi melempar buah persik gaib di Yomotsuhirasaka dan mengusir para pengejarnya.
statement.en: According to the various Kojiki and Nihongi accounts, Izanami ordered the "hags of Yomi" and the eight thunder kami to chase Izanagi; Izanagi threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka and thus dispersed his pursuers.

claims.quote: Fusu-ikazuchi: (Couchant thunder) Hono-ikazuchi: (Fire thunder) the Kojiki says that this kami came from Izanami's breasts.

statement.id: Daftar Wikipedia mencantumkan Fusu-ikazuchi (petir berbaring) dan Hono-ikazuchi (petir api); Kojiki menyebut Hono-ikazuchi berasal dari dada Izanami.
statement.en: The Wikipedia list gives Fusu-ikazuchi (couchant thunder) and Hono-ikazuchi (fire thunder); the Kojiki says Hono-ikazuchi came from Izanami's breasts.

claims.quote: Ō-ikazuchi: (Great thunder) both the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki state that Ō-ikazuchi came from Izanami's head.

statement.id: Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki sama-sama menyebut Ō-ikazuchi (petir besar) berasal dari kepala Izanami.
statement.en: Both the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki state that Ō-ikazuchi (great thunder) came from Izanami's head.

summary.en: The Nihon Shoki names the rectum.

topic.en: Placement of the eight thunders on Izanami's body

summary.id: Kojiki: kepala, dada, perut, kemaluan, tangan kiri, tangan kanan, kaki kiri, kaki kanan.
summary.en: Kojiki: head, breast, belly, genitals, left hand, right hand, left leg, right leg.

summary.id: Tulisan alternatif Nihongi: kepala, dada, perut, punggung, dubur, tangan, kaki, kemaluan, dengan sebagian nama berbeda; tiga cocok penuh, tiga hanya namanya, dua berbeda.
summary.en: Nihongi alternate writing: head, breast, belly, back, rectum, hands, feet, genitals, with some different names; three match fully, three in name only, two differ.
